text:
Colten Ellis did almost everything right for Buffalo on Wednesday. He faced 30 shots worth 3.14 expected goals and allowed two, saving 1.1 goals more than his workload deserved. It still wasn't enough, because Samuel Ersson was just as good at the other end and Ottawa found two goals in the last nine minutes for a 2-1 win that ended the Sabres' three-game winning streak.

Ottawa was the better team from the start. The Senators won the first period 1.02 to 0.66 in expected goals, the quality of each side's chances, and the second 1.10 to 0.56. Buffalo scored anyway. At 14:00 of the second, Peyton Krebs deflected in a shot, with Tage Thompson and Zach Benson assisting, and the Sabres' chance of winning rose from 52% to 73%.

For most of the next 20 minutes, Ellis made that lead look sturdy. Then Shane Pinto scored on a backhand at 11:33 of the third, set up by Philip Tomasino and Thomas Chabot, lifting Ottawa from a 16% chance of winning to 48%. Five minutes later Michael Amadio snapped home a Tim Stützle and Fabian Zetterlund setup at 16:51, and the Senators were at 90%. Stephen Halliday nearly made it 3-1 with a 24% look in the third that didn't go in.

Ersson earned the first star by stopping 23 of 24 and saving 1.05 goals more than expected. Ellis, a former Blues draft pick who posted a .922 save percentage in 42 AHL games two seasons ago, took the third star in a loss, which tells you how he played. Replay every shot and Ottawa wins 69% of the time.

The Senators also controlled the dots, winning 37 of 53 faceoffs, and Stützle played 23:06 with five shots on goal. Buffalo, which had been rolling, generated only 1.49 expected goals at even strength. Streaks end. The way this one ended, with a goalie stealing time until the dam broke, is the kind you can live with, but it's also a reminder of how much the Sabres leaned on him.
headline: Ottawa's late push beats Buffalo and a hot goalie
